boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Seton Hall rituals, annual gatherings and Pirate customs.

cards.title: Walk Around the Seal
cards.subtitle: University Green
cards.notes: Cross the Green by skirting the engraved seal; campus lore says stepping on it may delay graduation, a custom alumni recall from campus tours.
cards.short_summary: A long-running superstition centered on the granite seal at the Green’s center.
cards.evidence_claim: Seton Hall Magazine documents the custom of avoiding the University seal and says the tradition dates to before 1986.
cards.source_title: Things We Love About Seton Hall
cards.access_notes: The tradition concerns an outdoor campus landmark; follow current campus visitor guidance.

cards.title: Ask the Pirate for Luck
cards.subtitle: Pirate statue outside the Recreation Center
cards.notes: Pause by the Pirate statue and rub its foot for good luck before a test, paper or athletic event; the practice is described in Seton Hall orientation materials.
cards.short_summary: A touchable Pirate statue anchors a campus good-luck custom.
cards.evidence_claim: Seton Hall’s New Student Orientation page identifies rubbing the Pirate statue’s foot for good luck as a campus tradition.
cards.source_title: Life of a Pirate | New Student Orientation
cards.access_notes: Located by the Recreation Center; view it from public campus areas and respect facility access rules.

cards.title: Start the Year in a Sea of Blue
cards.subtitle: University Green
cards.notes: Join the start-of-year Blue Day carnival on the Green, wearing the event T-shirt and sampling the scheduled activities, inflatables and food-truck program.
cards.short_summary: Seton Hall’s welcome-back carnival turns the Green blue at the opening of the academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: Seton Hall’s orientation page calls Blue Day a campus tradition that kicks off the school year with a Green-based carnival.
cards.source_title: Life of a Pirate | New Student Orientation
cards.access_notes: Seton Hall reported the Blue Day carnival was free and open to all students; check the current orientation schedule for timing.

cards.entity_name: Christmas at the Hall Tree Lighting Ceremony
cards.title: Count Down to the Tree Lighting
cards.subtitle: University Green
cards.notes: Attend the annual early-December gathering on the Green and join the community countdown that marks the lighting of Seton Hall’s Christmas tree.
cards.short_summary: An Advent-season campus gathering built around a communal tree-lighting countdown.
cards.evidence_claim: Seton Hall describes Christmas at the Hall as an annual tree-lighting tradition and says attendees count down together to light the tree.
cards.source_title: 16th Annual Christmas at the Hall Tree Lighting to Illuminate Campus on December 2
cards.access_notes: This is a seasonal annual event; confirm the current year’s date and campus-access details before attending.

cards.entity_name: Christmas at the Hall Kick-off Mass
cards.title: Open Christmas at the Hall with Mass
cards.subtitle: Chapel of the Immaculate Conception
cards.notes: If it fits your practice, begin the Christmas at the Hall program at the Chapel before heading to the Green for the evening’s tree-lighting events.
cards.short_summary: The Christmas program opens with an annual campus Mass before the outdoor celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: Seton Hall’s 2025 Christmas at the Hall announcement says the annual program begins with a Kick-off Mass in the Chapel of the Immaculate Conception.
cards.source_title: 16th Annual Christmas at the Hall Tree Lighting to Illuminate Campus on December 2
cards.access_notes: A faith-based seasonal observance; participation is optional. Confirm the current service time with Campus Ministry.

cards.title: Gather for the Nativity Blessing
cards.subtitle: Christmas at the Hall program
cards.notes: Look for the Nativity blessing scheduled after the Kick-off Mass; it is a distinct part of the annual Christmas at the Hall sequence before the tree lighting.
cards.short_summary: A campus Nativity blessing connects Seton Hall’s holiday program to its Catholic identity.
cards.evidence_claim: Seton Hall’s Christmas at the Hall announcement states that the Kick-off Mass is followed by a blessing of the University Nativity Scene.
cards.source_title: 16th Annual Christmas at the Hall Tree Lighting to Illuminate Campus on December 2
cards.access_notes: Seasonal faith observance; check the current Christmas at the Hall schedule and location before attending.

cards.entity_name: St. Elizabeth Ann Seton Charter Day
cards.title: Mark Charter Day
cards.subtitle: Annual April campus celebration
cards.notes: Stop by the annual Charter Day program to reflect on Seton Hall’s founding and charter, and look for the student-facing treats-and-trivia portion of the day.
cards.short_summary: An annual commemoration of the University’s 1856 founding and 1861 state charter.
cards.evidence_claim: Seton Hall describes Charter Day as an annual tradition celebrating its 1856 founding and the 1861 granting of its New Jersey charter.
cards.source_title: St. Elizabeth Ann Seton Charter Day
cards.access_notes: The program is annual; the cited page lists the 2026 event. Check the University calendar for future details.

cards.title: Carry On Spirit Week
cards.subtitle: Campus-wide school-spirit programming
cards.notes: Watch the Student Alumni Association calendar for Spirit Week activities and take part in the scheduled events that build Pirate pride across the campus.
cards.short_summary: A school-spirit week introduced at Seton Hall by the Student Alumni Association.
cards.evidence_claim: Seton Hall states that its Student Alumni Association brought the tradition of Spirit Week to the University in its first year.
cards.access_notes: Programming varies by year; consult Student Alumni Association announcements for current activities.

cards.title: Process In with the Pipes
cards.subtitle: Baccalaureate Commencement
cards.notes: At Commencement, listen for the pipe band that opens the academic procession—a custom Seton Hall says honors Saint Elizabeth Ann Bayley Seton’s Scottish origins.
cards.short_summary: Bagpipes inaugurate Seton Hall’s graduation procession in tribute to its patroness.
cards.evidence_claim: Seton Hall states that it customarily begins the Commencement procession with a pipe band to honor Saint Elizabeth Ann Bayley Seton’s Scottish origins.
cards.source_title: Seton Hall Graduates 2,325 of the Class of 2026, Arthur Brooks Gives Commencement Address
cards.access_notes: This occurs as part of the University’s ticketed Commencement ceremony; follow official guest and venue instructions.

cards.title: Close Commencement with the Alma Mater
cards.subtitle: Baccalaureate Commencement
cards.notes: Stay through the close of Commencement to hear the University Alma Mater, the traditional final musical moment after graduates turn their tassels.
cards.short_summary: Seton Hall ends its Baccalaureate Commencement by singing the University Alma Mater.
cards.evidence_claim: Seton Hall’s report on the Class of 2026 says the Commencement ceremony closed, following tradition, with the singing of the University’s Alma Mater.
cards.source_title: Seton Hall Graduates 2,325 of the Class of 2026, Arthur Brooks Gives Commencement Address
cards.access_notes: Part of the University’s formal Commencement program; follow current event and venue instructions.
